newsitem.title: CHINA: FORECAST-China M2 seen up 24.5 percent in 1997.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-China M2 seen up 24.5 percent in 1997.

text.p: China's broad M2 money supply is forecast to rise a year-on-year 24.5 percent in 1997, the China Business Daily said on Friday.
China's M1, or cash in circulation plus current deposits, was expected to increase by a year-on-year 18 percent in 1997, the newspaper said, quoting unidentified sources.
The figures were set to complement targeted Gross Domestic Product growth of 10.5 percent in 1997, the newspaper said.
China's M2 and M1 grew by 25.3 percent and 18.9 percent respectively in 1996.
New loans extended by state-owned banks were forecast to reach 980 billion yuan ($118 billion) in 1997, it said.
Various types of loans extended by state banks were expected to total 5.72 trillion yuan at the end of 1997, up 20.7 percent from the year-ago period, the newspaper said.
